description:
# Problem
A callable argument bound to a contract type variable keeps the variable's BOUND instead of its INSTANTIATION, so escaping lambdas fail to specialize and lower as boxed ValueRef where they should be raw lanes.

# Repro (the disabled test)
compiler2_native_program_resource_fixture_shapes_callable_boundaries_explicitly (fixtures2/00026_make_resource.fz), red on baseline, currently red-worklist-disabled.

  extern "C" fn fz_make_resource(t, (t) -> nil) :: resource(t) when t: integer | cpointer
  fn make_resource(value, dtor), do: fz_make_resource(value, dtor)
  # @spec make_resource(t, (t) -> nil) :: resource(t) when t: integer | cpointer
  main: make_resource(42, fn (x) -> _resource_test_dtor(x) end)   # _resource_test_dtor: (integer) :: nil

# What the data proves
The dtor lambda body lowers with param_reprs = [ValueRef] but must be [RawInt]. `t` is ONE type variable; passing integer 42 in arg 1 BINDS t = integer for the whole call, forcing arg 2 to be exactly (integer) -> nil. `when t: integer | cpointer` is t's BOUND (allowed instantiations), not its type -- integer cannot become cpointer in the same instantiation.

# Why fz MUST specialize (vs Elixir)
Representation strategy is dictated by the runtime model. BEAM (../elixir): uniform boxed terms -> boxing required, specialization impossible; Dialyzer instantiates t only to VERIFY (idiomatic single spec: see agent.ex `get(agent,(state->a),timeout)::a when a: var`, file.ex `open!(...,(...->res))::res when res: var` -- one variable across callback + result, no two-spec split). fz: representation IS derived from type -> specialization required; leaving the dtor at ValueRef imports BEAM boxing into a system built to avoid it (information loss). Same spec, opposite mandatory outcomes. A two-spec split would be the wrong, redundant model.

# Old-world comparison (inspiration, NOT wholesale)
type_infer/mod.rs boundary_requests (l.839) types the lambda BOTTOM-UP from its body: it reads the closure's own inferred type (clo_ty -> callable_clauses -> clause.args) and activates the lambda at integer (from _resource_test_dtor(x)). The contract's bound is only verification. CORRECT INSIGHT. But it gets there via the full activation fixpoint (activate_request/merge_activation_inputs/enqueue, l.898-966) -- the machinery behind the fixpoint-oscillation/over-specialization pain compiler2 deliberately left behind. Take the insight, NOT the mechanism.

# compiler2 fix direction (machinery already exists)
contract.rs instantiate_match + Sigma already bind t from args and collect_arrow_subst RECURSES into arrow params; instantiated_match substitutes sigma into every param -- so (t)->nil with sigma{t:integer} CAN become (integer)->nil with no fixpoint. The hole is downstream: either apply() returns Underconstrained (t unbound -> bound used) OR the refined (integer)->nil input never reaches the escaping lambda's activation/param keying. Trace from refine_function_call_surface -> apply_function_contract -> refine_contract_inputs (semantic.rs:1399-1488) to where the dtor lambda's activation input type is set. Make the instantiated callable-param type drive the lambda's keying.

# Boundary ABI corollary (same test, separate facts)
Once the dtor body is RawInt, the runtime-facing callable boundary still faces the opaque uniform closure ABI: arg ValueRef (boundary unboxes to RawInt body), return Value(ValueRef) (dtor return never observed -- runtime discards it; rides the boxed nil seam). So the test's CURRENT assertions enshrine a pre-collapse model and must be re-aimed on fix:
  boundary arg_reprs: [RawInt] -> [ValueRef]   (boundary faces surface; body is the raw lane)
  boundary return_abi: stays Value(ValueRef)   (boxed nil seam; never used)
  body param_reprs:   stays [RawInt]           (the specialization this ticket delivers)
boundary_return_abi (artifact.rs:2520) currently passes through Value{repr}; whether first-class boundaries should uniformly box the return (ValueRef-facing per fz-hwn.16 point 6) is a sub-question to settle here, NOT in .16. An earlier boundary_return_abi boxing experiment was reverted pending this ticket.

# NOT fz-hwn.16
.16 (resume/return transport collapse) is complete and green. This is a distinct contract/type-variable-instantiation concern, discovered while re-enabling resource_fixture from the red-worklist.

comments.text:
GROUND-TRUTH ROOT (instrumented, then reverted) -- corrects earlier guesses:

The escaping lambda's ACTIVATION is keyed with the UN-INSTANTIATED contract type variable, not the instantiation and not the body-inferred type.

Evidence (make_resource fixture 00026):
- [TYIN] dump of key.activation.input per executable:
  - make_resource/fz_make_resource (arity 2): input[0] = Ty(17):RawInt  -> arg 1 specialized to integer CORRECTLY (t=integer bound from 42).
  - dtor lambda (arity 1): input[0] = Ty(21):ValueRef.
- [CTR] dump of the make_resource contract arrow: params=[Ty(21), Ty(22)], param_has_vars=[true,true], constraints=[alpha0]. So Ty(21) IS alpha0 -- the raw type variable `t` itself, NOT the bound integer|cpointer. abi_value_repr(free var) = ValueRef.

So: the type var `t` is preserved in the contract (NOT baked to its bound -- earlier spec-resolution hypothesis WRONG). The substitution machinery is correct: Descr::instantiate (descr.rs:274 walked_funcs) DOES recurse into arrow args/ret, so (Var t)->nil with sigma{t:integer} WOULD become (integer)->nil. The make_resource call DOES bind t=integer (arg1 -> Ty(17)).

The defect: the escaping lambda's activation is materialized from the contract's GENERIC callable parameter `(t)->nil` carrying the free var `t` (Ty(21)=alpha0), instead of the INSTANTIATED `(integer)->nil` (Ty(17)) or the body-inferred type (x: integer from _resource_test_dtor(x)). A lambda activation whose input is a free spec variable can only lower to ValueRef.

FIX LOCATION: where compiler2 materializes the escaping callable's activation input types (the demand-closure callable materialization / callable_executables_from_type and the surface that feeds it). Two correct options:
(a) instantiate the callable param with the call-site sigma (t=integer) before keying the escaping activation, OR
(b) key the escaping lambda from its OWN body-inferred type (x: integer), the old-world insight (type_infer boundary_requests reads the closure's own clause.args) WITHOUT old-world's activation-fixpoint machinery.

DOMINANCE: this is plausibly the dominant typing root behind the worklist. Reducers (Enum.reduce `(acc,elem)->acc` etc.) are callables bound to Enum's spec type vars in arrow positions -- same shape. If their activations carry free vars, the type fixpoint can't settle -> the ~18 reducer/enum HANGS, and starves LowerNativeProgram of concrete types -> the ~10 LowerNativeProgram fatals. Worklist root-cluster triage: 41 assert_resolved (split into ExpandFunctionSource macros ~12, LowerNativeProgram ~10, ScopeCode 2), 9 original_entry_ids, 3 unbound-value, 18 hangs, ~12 singletons -> ~6 roots; types upstream of lowering upstream of codegen, so fixing this typing root should cascade-clear the lowering/hang clusters. Macros (~12) are an orthogonal sibling subsystem, not in this pipeline.

FINAL PLAN (root dump-confirmed; shovel-ready).

ROOT (confirmed via `fz dump --emit specs` -- I should have used this from the start instead of eprintln):
  ; spec Kernel.make_resource(2)  key: [int, (a0) -> a1]
  ;   Var(2) :: &fn190[]:(a12160) -> a12223           <- dtor lambda: closure-lit with FREE VARS
  ;   callee_key=[42, &fn190[]:(a12160) -> a12223]
A lambda with untyped params gets a closure-lit type carrying free type variables for param/return. The make_resource contract application DOES instantiate correctly (instrumented: KNOWN -> matched params [Ty(17)=integer, Ty(31)=(integer)->nil]); but that grounded surface only keys the CALLEE's activation -- it is never written back to ground the lambda VALUE's type in the caller's value_types. So the demand-closure escaping-callable materialization (runtime_demand.rs callable_executables_from_type:1172) reads the free-var closure-lit, specializes clause.args = [free var], keys the dtor activation with a free var, and abi_value_repr(free var) = ValueRef. Old-world carries the SAME free-var lambda at spec level but grounds it via its activation fixpoint; compiler2 dropped that fixpoint and never re-grounds -> the defect.

INVARIANT (data-model-up): an activation key's input types are GROUND -- a free type variable in an activation input is illegal/unrepresentable.

STEPS (simple, targeted, correct-by-construction):
1. Ground the escaping callable's type at the CONSUMING call: when a callable value is passed to a function whose contract instantiation is KNOWN, write the grounded callable-arg surface (Ty(31)) back to the caller's value_types for that callable value. Then callable_executables_from_type reads a ground type and keys the lambda activation on integer -> RawInt. (The binding already exists -- contract.apply returns it KNOWN; it just is not propagated to the value.) Principle: the callee body constrains the var, the expected type binds it -- never overwrite the param with the bound, never leave it free.
2. Lock the invariant: debug_assert at callable_executables_from_type that the materialized activation inputs have no free vars. Add AFTER step 1 (before, it would panic across the suite). Turns silent ValueRef-fallback into a loud failure so the class cannot regress.
3. Guidepost: add a compiler2 `--dump activations` kind (mirroring old-world `fz dump --emit specs`) exposing each activation's ground/free-var input types, so this is one command to inspect, not eprintln. Pin resource_fixture + one reducer as telemetry/dump-observing tests.

VERIFY (cascade is the proof): resource_fixture dtor body -> RawInt (re-aim its boundary assertions: arg ValueRef faces the surface, return Value(ValueRef) is the never-used boxed seam); re-enable one reducer (enum_reduce_runtime_graph_reducer) -> it SETTLES (no hang); sweep the worklist and watch the ~18 reducer hangs + ~10 LowerNativeProgram fatals clear off this one typing fix (types upstream of lowering upstream of codegen).

REMOVE: the free-var -> ValueRef silent fallback path.
SCOPE GUARD: macros (~12) are a sibling subsystem, not in this fix.

Banked commits on branch: 54a4bead5 (fz-hwn.16 resume collapse), 1b8faa05d (red-test worklist baseline + nextest isolation). Suite green 2158/0/81-skipped.

title: Compiler2: instantiate extern/contract type variables into callable parameters (escaping lambda specialization)
